decision: The internal platform and the Correspondence Gateway portal use SEPARATE proof ledgers. Taken by the platform owner on 2026-09-24, reversing an argument this repository made for sharing one list divided by a Purpose value.
whyItMatters: A shared list is separated by a WHERE clause. A filter that is edited, generated wrongly, or omitted in a flow written later reads across the boundary, and only npm run test:proofidentity would notice. A separate list makes the boundary structural: there is nothing to cross.
whatIsBlocked: One value. scripts/build-identification-phase4.mjs reads listId from this file and uses it the moment it is set: the proof mint (OTP_VERIFY__IP_OTP_VERIFY__4dbe6dde) writes there and every identification package reads there. Until then they use the shared ledger and its internal-session Purpose filter, which is the arrangement this decision supersedes. A GUID cannot be invented here; a package naming a list that does not exist fails at run time. (The DGO_* generator that read this file before 2026-10-06 is retired.)

listToProvision.title: DGO_SessionProofs
listToProvision.whyThatSite: Internal identity already lives there — DGO_UserDirectory and DGO_RoleCatalogue are on the governance site, and a session proof is an identity artefact. The portal's ledger stays where it is, on Global_Digital_Documents_Centre.

columns.holds: the proof token itself, an opaque GUID
the directory address the proof was issued to; this is what the endpoints read the caller from
'internal-session'. Retained even with a separate list: it costs nothing and keeps the filter that makes the boundary checkable
when the proof dies. Four hours after issue, per AUTHENTICATION_CONTRACT.md §2a
false on issue. Setting it true is how a single proof is revoked without a key rotation

listToProvision.whyIndexTitle: Every endpoint call does one lookup filtered on Title. Unindexed, that is a full-list scan on the hot path of every authenticated request in the estate.

howToApplyIt: 1. Create the list above on the governance site with those six columns, and index Title.
2. Put its GUID in listId here.
3. npm run internalpaste && npm run flowvars — the eight internal packages rebuild against it.
4. Reinstall those eight packages per docs/deployment/RUNBOOK.md.
5. npm run test:proofidentity turns the AWAITING_PROVISIONING warning into a pass.
untilThen: The internal flows read the portal's ledger filtered on Purpose eq 'internal-session', and every one of them carries that filter — npm run test:proofidentity asserts it on each. The separation holds today; it is one clause wide rather than structural, which is what this decision changes.
